findings.title: Google Calendar credential.key is overwritten with a Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` in the database becomes `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, so the next time `GoogleCalendarService` is constructed `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) will throw a `ZodError` and break Google Calendar for that user.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]` instead of a dynamic key validator
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `z.string().toString()` at module load time, producing the literal property key `"[object Object]"`. Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` requires a numeric property literally named `"[object Object]"` and strips every other property (such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, etc.). As a result, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will always fail validation with `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` unless the response happens to contain `"[object Object]": <number>`, and even then all expiry fields will be stripped.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, which is incompatible with SDK/axios callers
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. However, several callers expect the return shape of their own client library rather than a Fetch `Response`: `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data.access_token`, `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `tokenInfo.data` (Axios response), and `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` directly off the returned object. None of these properties exist on a Fetch `Response`, so token refresh with credential syncing enabled will fail or write `undefined` tokens into the database for Google Calendar, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, and Zoho CRM.

findings.title: Salesforce CalendarService references `prisma` without importing it and uses stale access_token
findings.body: `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce calendar operation. In addition, line 75 refreshes the token via `fetch(...)` on every `getClient` call without using `refreshOAuthTokens`, and line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)`.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the third argument to be `userId: number | null` and sends it as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (`credential.id`) is passed instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the credential's primary key rather than the Cal.com user ID.

findings.title: Looking up `appStoreMetadata` by `app.slug` fails for apps whose key in `appStoreMetadata` differs from their slug
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by the app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `zoomvideo`, `larkcalendar`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` and `appMetadata.slug` use the config slug (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `zoom`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` on line 50 returns `undefined` for all of these apps and causes the webhook to respond with 404 `"App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`.
